claim: Let \(g\ge2\), let \(p\) be prime, and let \(A/\mathbb F_{p^2}\) be an abelian variety of dimension \(g\). For the one-sign maximality test that samples uniform \(P\in A(\mathbb F_{p^2})\) and accepts when \([p+1]P=0\), every non-maximal \(A\) has false-positive probability at most \(B_g(p)=\min\{1,((p+1)^{2g}-(p-1)^{2g})/(p-1)^{2g}\}\); the analogous one-sign minimality test with \([p-1]P=0\) satisfies the same bound. For \(g\ge2\), the proof of Theorem 4.1 in arXiv:2610.01924v1 does not obtain its displayed threshold \(4gp^{2g-1}\) from the cited width lemma, because the exact Hasse--Weil width is \((p+1)^{2g}-(p-1)^{2g}>4gp^{2g-1}\). Replacing that step by the exact width repairs the stated \(O(p^{-1})\) conclusion; \(k\) independent repetitions of one sign have error at most \(B_g(p)^k\).
integrity: The all-dimension argument is symbolic and uses only the exact Hasse--Weil interval, subgroup divisibility, and a binomial expansion. The companion verifier uses exact integer/rational arithmetic as a regression check; no numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The result repairs the width-based proof and supplies a rigorous universal branchwise probability bound. It does not establish optimality, does not rule out a separate structural proof of the smaller threshold used in the source, and does not analyze acceptance of both signs as a single union event.
title: Exact-width repair of the any-dimensional extremality test
